title: Mental Health & Substance Use Prevention
before:
School interdisciplinary teams (administrators, educators, school counselors, mental health professionals, and school nurses) are charged with the responsibility of fostering systems that enhance all realms of student education including social and emotional learning, mental well-being, and substance use prevention. Teams must identify priorities and create an infrastructure that supports the growing needs of our students and school communities. The resources provided on this page are intended to support education professionals in the evaluation of school health programs, identification of priorities and action planning, as well as provision of specific education resources for students, staff, and families.

  • American Academy of Pediatrics: Health Services Assessment Tool for Schools (HATS)

notes: 2 section headers — too few for a contents list.

decisions.label: Rebuild the heading outline
decisions.why: 2 headings sit at a level the page never opens — "School Health Program Evaluation and Action Plan" is an h4 with no h3 above it, so it is neither announced nor styled as the sub-section it is. Each heading moves to one level below whatever encloses it.

decisions.label: Turn the headings into section headers
decisions.why: 2 headings are plain text where every other page uses a section header, so the page reads as one continuous wall instead of parts.

decisions.label: Write the email addresses the same way
decisions.why: 1 address is shown in whatever case it was typed in. The house form capitalises each name and leaves a middle initial in lower case — emily.poland@maine.gov → Emily.Poland@maine.gov. Only the first letter of each part changes, so a name that spells itself LaBreck keeps doing so.

decisions.label: Draw a closing link as the action it is
decisions.why: 1 passage ends with a paragraph holding nothing but a link — the thing the passage was leading up to. Set as running text it looks like any other link in the sentence above it. The site already has one way of drawing an action, so it takes that. The words do not change.

decisions.label: Use this paragraph as the page description
decisions.why: It is the page’s own opening paragraph, moved into the banner rather than rewritten.
